title: Map of Roman Britain and the tribes
subject: History
unit: Summer 1: The Roman Empire and Roman Britain (Flow)
source: Written for history/y3 lesson 15 (Map of Roman Britain and the tribes (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 15: The Romans invade Britain, AD 43. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.text: Colour the tribes' lands using the slides and draw the main Roman roads as straight lines between the towns.

panels.title: Why Britain?
points: Metals: tin, lead, silver and gold

blocks.title: Sort into: Made peace / Fought back
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Made peace, Fought back.
blocks.answer: Made peace: kept their land; traded with Rome. Fought back: Caratacus; Boudica's revolt

parts.text: Point: I think they should make peace
Reason: the army was very strong
Because: they could keep their homes

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: A choice with a reason and a 'but'

keywords.def: an army entering a country to take it
a group of families with a leader
a part of the empire ruled by Rome
a friend who helps in war

questions.q: Who was emperor when Rome invaded Britain?
Name a leader who fought the Romans.
Core: In the portal response box, write as a tribal leader in AD 43: will you make peace or fight? Start 'I have decided to... because...' and give two reasons.
questions.a: A clear choice with two historical reasons, e.g. peace to keep our land and trade

questions.q: Extend: Add one thing your tribe might lose by your choice.
questions.a: For example: peace means paying taxes; fighting risks lives and homes

questions.q: Stretch: Why did Boudica rebel even after years of Roman rule?
questions.a: The Romans treated the Iceni badly and took their land and wealth
A) AD 43. Claudius invaded in AD 43; the Romans left around AD 410.

questions.q: Big question: fight, run or make friends?
questions.a: A choice with reasons about safety, freedom and the Roman army's strength
